sourceCoverage.chapterCharacter: Qingshigao geography treatise 28 (地理二十八): the Chahar Eight Banners. A five-sentence historical preface (s0006-s0010) names the only five people: the Little Prince (元裔小王子), Buxi (布希), Ligdan Khan (林丹汗), his son 孔果爾額哲 and Burne (布爾呢). The rest gives each banner's seat, distance to the capital, Ming/Han antecedents, borders, mountains and waters.
sourceCoverage.readMethod: Every unit's Chinese, literal and idiomatic field read in full. Each repeated formula (距京師, 牧廠, 蒙名 lists) and every transliterated place name was checked across all of its uses. Qingshigao is not in the Siku Quanshu, so the cross-checks use the same history's other chapters at the staging revision (Taizong annals 002, Zhili geography 054, biography 251, Fanbu 520).
mechanicalChecks: All nine 東南距京師 units checked against latitude/longitude (s0015 42°20′ N, s0016 west of the capital meridian; capital 39°55′ at Qingshigao 054 s0076) and the stated bearings from Zhangjiakou/Dushikou.
Each name in the people preface checked against the Qingshigao annals for event ownership and year.

substantiveFindings.summary: 44 English field defects in 22 units. Every 東南距京師 distance is inverted to "southeast of the capital" (9 units, both fields). 牧廠 is rendered "pasture office" (5 units), and 內務府 is called the "Interior Ministry" (s0117). 編為佐領 makes the surrendered Khalkha/Oirat "assistant commandants" (s0011), and 元裔 gains an unsupported "collateral" (s0006). Kuisu Pool becomes a Mongol name of Red Salt Pool (s0084). Ejei's name is unsupported as romanized (s0009, F3), and four place names are garbled (s0036, s0068, s0096, s0105).

The extraction dates Ligdan Khan's death (claim-12) and Khongor Ejei's submission, banner enrollment and attestation (claims 19-21) to AD 1632 at year precision. In s0008 天聰六年 dates only the campaign and the flight. The Qingshigao Taizong annals report Ligdan's death in Tiancong 8 (002 s0716 言其汗林丹病殂) and the receipt of Ejei in Tiancong 9 (002 s0755, s0763). The fresh audit marked these items supported; this is new cross-chapter evidence, not a repeat review.

substantiveFindings.summary: p004 孔果爾額哲 is displayed as "Kökege Erjen", a form matching neither 孔果爾 (Khongor) nor 額哲 (Ejei). Its plain-pinyin element "Kongguer Eizhe" also misspells the name claim's own Kǒngguǒ'ěr Ézhé. The corpus records the same man as Ejei / Ejei Khongor (qingshigao 216, 227).
substantiveFindings.resolution: scopedChronologyOrIdentityChanges C4 with the s0009 English repair

definiteTranslationRepairs.zh: 察哈爾八旗：東南距京師四百三十里。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: Chahar Eight Banners: four hundred thirty li southeast of the capital.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: Chahar Eight Banners: the capital lies four hundred thirty li to the southeast.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 東南距京師N里 states that the capital lies N li to the southeast; it is the treatise's formula for places northwest of Beijing. Both English fields invert it, putting every banner "southeast of the capital". The chapter itself places Chahar beyond the Xuanhua/Datong frontier (s0005), at 42°20′ N (s0015) against the capital's 39°55′ (Qingshigao 054 s0076, Shuntian), and west of the capital's meridian (s0016); each banner lies north or northwest of Zhangjiakou or Dushikou.

definiteTranslationRepairs.zh: 東界正白旗察哈爾，西界正黃旗察哈爾，南界鑲黃旗牧廠，北界蘇尼特右翼，廣一百六十里，袤一百九十里。
definiteTranslationRepairs.before: On the east it borders Plain White Banner Chahar, on the west Plain Yellow Banner Chahar, on the south the Bordered Yellow Banner pasture office, on the north Sunite Right Wing; one hundred sixty li wide and one hundred ninety li long.
definiteTranslationRepairs.after: On the east it borders Plain White Banner Chahar, on the west Plain Yellow Banner Chahar, on the south the Bordered Yellow Banner pasture grounds, on the north Sunite Right Wing; one hundred sixty li wide and one hundred ninety li long.
definiteTranslationRepairs.reason: 牧廠 is a pasture ground (here the Army Ministry, Bordered Yellow Banner and Imperial Household herd pastures), a tract that can form a banner's boundary; "pasture office" makes the boundary an office. Every use is repaired.
